verdict.rationale: Termius documents its own secure access to servers wherever they live: SSH, Mosh, Telnet and Serial connections, jump hosts, all three port-forwarding types, FIDO2/MFA and biometric keys, and Cloud Sync of AWS, DigitalOcean and Azure instances. Nothing in the evidence shows native Kubernetes cluster access, which the story explicitly names. missing for 10: native Kubernetes cluster access (kubectl/exec/cluster discovery), any evidence covering non-SSH resource types such as databases, independent hands-on corroboration of access across cloud resources.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get secure infrastructure access to resources wherever they live, including Kubernetes clusters

citations.quote: It includes a built-in Local terminal and supports SSH, Mosh, Telnet, Serial, and SFTP.
if you configure a jump host for a Group, every Host within it will automatically connect through that jump host
Termius supports all three main types of port forwarding (local, remote, and dynamic)
You can enable Cloud Sync for a specific group and integrate it with AWS, DigitalOcean, or Azure. Once the setup is completed, Termius syncs the matching instances
Secure SSH authentication with FIDO2 security keys and MFA.
Secure connections with device-bound keys and biometric protection with Windows Hello, Touch ID/Face ID, or Android biometrics.
